items.title: Transport along a pair path in a doubly dependent family agrees with the composite of the two transports

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 1712-1723: for a doubly dependent family and a pair path, the transport in the uncurried family is the equivalence obtained by univalence from the composite of two transports. The proof (source lines 1724-1726) is a single path induction, but it is the complete argument for this comparison rather than a pointer to another result: after the induction both compared functions reduce to the identity, because the coherence path and both transports become reflexivity. What the card counts is the comparison itself, whose content lies in the statement: identifying the two transports, exhibiting the coherence path and invoking the action of the dependent function on the identification. The reduction step is recorded verbatim and the statement carries the substance.
